counterhypotheses.claim: Put inferred effects directly into lexical binding identity.
counterhypotheses.result: Rejected in the tested pipeline because it introduces a dependency cycle and identity churn under effect-only mutations.

counterhypotheses.claim: Use overload identity (name + full signature) as the default source-level binding policy.
counterhypotheses.result: Exact typed calls resolved in 20,000/20,000 proxy cases, but partial-type calls were ambiguous in the constructed 20,000/20,000 discriminating cases; no current BASE requirement justifies default overload complexity.

counterhypotheses.claim: Include runtime capabilities in callable semantic identity to increase safety.
counterhypotheses.result: Runtime capability is invocation authority, not program meaning; safety requires fresh authorization rather than static identity amplification.

hypotheses.claim: Lexical BindingKey should be based on module/scope plus exact symbol identity and must exclude inferred effect summaries and runtime capability context.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production compiler design that includes inferred effects in binding identity yet remains acyclic, deterministic, incrementally stable and diagnostically simpler.
hypotheses.prediction: Effect-summary changes leave BindingKey stable; adding inferred effect closure as a BindingKey dependency creates a Resolve/CallGraph/EffectClosure cycle.

hypotheses.claim: ClayCode needs separate identity layers for BindingKey, FunctionTypeId, DefinitionSemanticId and provenance/ABI-bound ContractId.
hypotheses.falsifier: A fewer-layer scheme that preserves exact resolution, semantic equivalence, replay integrity and incremental invalidation under the same mutation matrix.
hypotheses.prediction: Rename, signature, body, provenance and ABI mutations affect different identity layers without cross-contaminating unrelated layers.

hypotheses.claim: For BASE, same-scope duplicate source names should fail closed unless a concrete application counterexample requires overload resolution.
hypotheses.falsifier: A mandatory BASE application or FRANK slice that cannot be expressed ergonomically/correctly without overloading.
hypotheses.prediction: Unique-name resolution avoids partial-type ambiguity while remaining sufficient for current G9/FRANK callable needs.

hypotheses.claim: Declared effect contracts may be part of a callable static contract/type if fixed before effect inference; inferred effect summaries remain analysis outputs checked against that declaration.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production SCC inference demonstrating declared effect contracts necessarily destabilize binding or cannot conservatively bound effects.
hypotheses.prediction: Recursive effect inference remains acyclic and BindingKey stable; exceeding declared effect bounds is rejected.

hypotheses.claim: Replay/effect receipts should bind at least the resolved DefinitionSemanticId plus emitted artifact/ContractId, not BindingKey alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: A replay system proving BindingKey-only receipts cannot misattribute changed implementations across rebuilds/ABI changes.
hypotheses.prediction: Body or ABI changes invalidate replay compatibility even when the lexical symbol name is unchanged.
